China gold market update: Robust demand in October

PDF
0.23 mb

HighlightsBoth the LBMA Gold Price PM in USD and the Shanghai Benchmark Gold Price PM (SHAUPM) in RMB extended their September weakness into October; gold’s rebound in early November proved short-lived, with prices later falling to the lowest y-t-d.1Chinese gold ETFs saw a fourth consecutive monthly inflow in October, pushing total holdings to a month-end record; yet outflows have emerged so far in November amid the gold price weakness2Gold futures trading at the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) cooled further Gold withdrawals from the Shanghai Gold Exchange (SGE) strengthened unseasonally m/m, underpinned mainly by healthy bullion investment; meanwhile, jewellers’ replenishment remained activeThe People’s Bank of China (PBoC) reported a 26t gold addition during October, the largest in three years and the 24th consecutive monthly buying.Looking aheadBullion investment may continue to be supported by the current macro backdrop, although a recovery in the equity market – should it persist – may divert some attention away from gold ETFs. Jewellery consumption could continue to improve, supported by seasonality and lower prices may further boost buying.

Gold fell further in OctoberGold continued to retreat (Chart 1). The LBMA Gold Price PM in USD and the SHAUPM in RMB fell 6.3% and 5.9%, respectively. A rotation of funds out of equities and gold futures into bonds could be a key driver of gold’s weakness during the month. The additional weakness in the USD gold price is likely due to heavier selling pressure in US trading – with both COMEX gold futures and US gold ETFs experiencing pull backs. October’s weakness brought gold’s y-t-d loss to 7.1% in USD and 9.4% in RMB, respectively – the sharp appreciation in the RMB against the dollar has been a key factor behind the relative weakness.Gold began to rebound in early November post the US mid-terms and fell later amid changing expectations of the Fed’s actions. In the near term, shifting expectations of the Fed’s future policy path in response to economic data releases will continue to influence the gold market sentiment. But exactly how the mid-term election results and policy changes will impact gold remains to be seen.

Chart 1: Gold continued to retreat Monthly gold price performance in USD and RMB*

*Data to 31 October 2026. Based on the LBMA Gold Price PM in USD and the Shanghai Benchmark Gold Price PM in RMB. Source: Shanghai Gold Exchange, ICE Benchmark Administration, World Gold Council

Chinese gold ETFs have seen inflows four months in a rowChinese gold ETFs expanded for the fourth consecutive month, adding 6.3t (RMB5.3bn, US$784mn) in October. This lifted their total holdings to a month-end record of 310t, with 62t added so far in 2026 (Chart 2). But Chinese gold ETFs’ total AUM fell 4% to RMB265bn (US$40bn) as a lower gold price more than offset the healthy monthly tonnage inflow.Similar to previous months, Chinese investors’ strategic allocation to gold ETFs was supported by equity market weakness, low government bond yields, and encouragement from the local central bank’s non-stop gold purchasing announcements.In early November gold ETFs reversed their earlier momentum and saw modest outflows; measures to stabilise the equity market3 – and the subsequent stabilisation – may have diverted local investor interest away from gold. The gold price weakness later in the month also deterred investors. 

Chart 2: Chinese gold ETF holdings have risen at their second ever fastest pace, y-t-d Chinese gold ETFs’ monthly cumulative tonnage demand* 

*Data to 31 October 2026.Source: Company filings, World Gold Council

Gold futures trading less activeActivity in China’s gold futures market softened further in October (Chart 3). The average daily trading volume on the SHFE fell 28% m/m to 258t/day, while net longs held by the top 20 market participants, based on available data, declined 15t from the end of September to 134t, but remained 31% higher y/y. The weakening gold price and lower volatility led to less bullish positioning and softer trading.

Chart 3: Gold futures trading volumes and net longs fell alongside the gold priceTop 20 net longs of SHFE’s gold futures and average daily trading volumes* 

*Data to 31 October 2026.Source: Shanghai Futures Exchange, World Gold Council 

Another October of unseasonal wholesale demand strengthWholesale demand for gold has defied normal seasonal patterns. Usually, jewellers’ replenishment demand lowers after strong restocking in September thereby impacting the overall wholesale demand in October. But gold withdrawals from the SGE rose by a mild 2% m/m to 94t in October (Chart 4). This was mainly driven by:An improvement in bullion sales as lower gold prices triggered dip-buying activities. Investor confidence continued to be buoyed by the PBoC’s non-stop gold purchases, while recent heightened equity market volatility, lowering yields and a lack of attractive investment alternatives sustained investor allocation to goldActive restocking by jewellers amid the gold price dip and encouragement from healthy consumption during the National Day Holiday early in the month.4Even so, wholesale gold demand in October remained subdued, at 24% lower y/y, due mainly to the notable y/y weakness in the jewellery sector.The October rebound in gold withdrawals is not unprecedented: a similar pattern occurred in 2025 alongside strong bar and coin demand. In our view, this reflects a broader shift in China’s wholesale gold market, with investment demand increasingly replacing jewellery consumption as the key driver of withdrawals. This transition began in 2025 and strengthened in 2026, driven by cautious discretionary spending and higher value-preservation demand in the current economic cycle, as well as the VAT reform in late 2025, which benefited bullion buying. Bar and coin investment in 2025 notably exceeded jewellery consumption for the first time in history, and the same is true so far in 2026, making traditional jewellery-driven seasonal patterns less apparent in aggregate withdrawals.

Chart 4: Wholesale demand improved unseasonally m/m in October Gold withdrawals from the SGE by month and the ten-year monthly average*

*As of 31 October 2026. Ten-year average based on data between 2016 and 2025.  Source: Shanghai Gold Exchange, World Gold Council 

The PBoC reported larger gold buyingThe PBoC announced a 26t gold accumulation in October, the highest monthly buying since October 2023 (Chart 5). Official gold holdings have now risen for 24 consecutive months, reaching 2,435t, 8.1% of FX reserves, down from 8.5% in September. This decline is largely reflective of the pullback in gold prices during the month, as the value of gold reserves contracted 5.3% despite the notable tonnage addition.

Chart 5: The PBoC accelerated its gold purchase in October amid declining pricesThe PBoC’s reported gold purchases and the gold price*

*Data to 31 October 2026.Source: State Administration of Foreign Exchanges, World Gold Council

Gold imports rose further in SeptemberChina’s gold imports increased further to 129t in September, 5t higher than August and up 41% y/y, extending the recovery seen over previous months. The improvement was likely underpinned by seasonal strong wholesale demand ahead of the peak season and favourable import incentives from the rising local gold price premium.

Chart 6: Gold imports continued to rise in SeptemberNet gold imports under HS7108*

*Data to September 2026.Source: China Customs, World Gold Council
